Aragonese

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French bicyclette.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /biθiˈkleta/
  • IPA(key): /bisiˈkleta/ (Benasquese)
  • Syllabification: bi‧ci‧cle‧ta
  • Rhymes: -eta

Noun

[edit]

bicicleta f

  1. bicycle

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • becicleta

Derived terms

[edit]
  • bicicleta de montanya
  • bicicleta estatica
  • mancha de bicicleta

Related terms

[edit]
  • bici
  • tricicle

Portuguese

[edit]
Portuguese Wikipedia has an article on:
bicicleta
Wikipedia pt

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • biciclete

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French bicyclette, from Latin bi- (“two”) +‎ Ancient Greek κύκλος (kúklos, “circle, wheel”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
 
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /bi.siˈklɛ.tɐ/
  • (Brazil) IPA(key): /bi.siˈklɛ.tɐ/
    • (Southern Brazil) IPA(key): /bi.siˈklɛ.ta/
  • (Portugal) IPA(key): /bi.siˈklɛ.tɐ/, /bɨ.siˈklɛ.tɐ/

  • Rhymes: -ɛtɐ
  • Hyphenation: bi‧ci‧cle‧ta

Noun

[edit]

bicicleta f (plural bicicletas)

  1. bicycle (vehicle)
  2. (soccer) bicycle kick (a kick in which the kicker leans backwards and kicks the ball back over his head)
    Synonyms: (Brazil) chute de bicicleta, (Portugal) pontapé de bicicleta

Derived terms

[edit]
  • bici
  • bicicleta de montanha
  • bicicleta ergométrica
  • bicicleta estática
  • bicicletaria
  • bicicletário
  • bicicleteiro
  • bicicletinha
  • bicicletona
  • biciclizar
  • bicla

Related terms

[edit]
  • biciclo

Further reading

[edit]
  • “bicicleta”, in Dicionário Aulete Digital (in Portuguese), Rio de Janeiro: Lexikon Editora Digital, 2008–2026
  • “bicicleta”, in Dicionário infopédia da Lingua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Porto: Porto Editora, 2003–2026
  • “bicicleta”, in Michaelis Dicionário Brasileiro da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), São Paulo: Editora Melhoramentos, 2015–2026, →ISBN
  • “bicicleta”, in Dicionário Priberam da Língua Portuguesa (in Portuguese), Lisbon: Priberam, 2008–2026

bicicleta f

Spanish

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French bicyclette, from Latin bi- (“two”) + Ancient Greek κύκλος (kúklos, “circle, wheel”).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /biθiˈkleta/ [bi.θiˈkle.t̪a] (Equatorial Guinea, Spain)
  • IPA(key): /bisiˈkleta/ [bi.siˈkle.t̪a] (Latin America, Philippines)
  • Audio (Colombia):(file)
  • Rhymes: -eta
  • Syllabification: bi‧ci‧cle‧ta

Noun

[edit]

bicicleta f (plural bicicletas)

  1. (exercise, vehicles) bicycle, pushbike, cycle
    Synonyms: bici; see also Thesaurus:bicicleta
    andar/montar en bicicleta ― to ride a bike
  2. (soccer) step over, pedalada (a dribbling move, or feint, in football (soccer), used to fool a defensive player into thinking the offensive player, in possession of the ball, is going to move in a direction he does not intend to move in)
  3. (climbing) bicycle

Usage notes

[edit]
  • (soccer): Bicicleta is a false friend and does not mean bicycle kick. The Spanish word for bicycle kick is chilena.

Hyponyms

[edit]
  • bicicleta balona
  • bicicleta de montaña
  • bicicleta de reparto
  • bicicleta elíptica
  • bicicleta estática
  • bicicleta fija (“exercise bike”)

Derived terms

[edit]
  • aparcabicicletas
  • bici
  • bicicleta financiera
  • bicicletada
  • si mi abuela tuviera ruedas, sería una bicicleta

Related terms

[edit]
  • triciclo

Descendants

[edit]
  • → Cebuano: bisikleta
  • → Hiligaynon: bisikleta
  • → Tagalog: bisikleta

[edit]
